mainTopic: Prayer lessons from חזקיהו and the woman from שונם, the late time for קריאת שמע, and the position for saying שמע
overview: This amud starts with prayer. רבי חנן teaches that even if a dream says you will die tomorrow, you should keep praying. חזקיהו did exactly this: he turned to the wall and prayed. The גמרא explains the 'wall' and his prayer, lists six things he did (three the חכמים approved and three they did not), and explains his leap-year mistake on the thirtieth of אדר. It then teaches that one who relies on his own merit is answered through others' merit, and the reverse, using משה and חזקיהו as examples. Next come lessons from the story of the woman from שונם and אלישע: the room she built, accepting gifts, and the value of hosting a תלמיד חכם. A series of prayer rules follows: pray from a low place, keep your feet together, and do not eat before praying. The גמרא returns to the משנה, ruling like רבי יהושע and discussing whether a late reader of שמע still says the ברכות. Finally, a new משנה brings the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל about what position to be in for שמע, and the story of רבי טרפון.

steps.title: Even a dream of death should not stop a person from praying
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנן teaches that even if a dream tells a person he will die tomorrow, he should still pray for רחמים. He proves it from a פסוק in קהלת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנן said: Even if the master of dreams tells a person that tomorrow he will die, he should not hold himself back from praying for mercy. As it says: 'For in the multitude of dreams and vanities there are many words; but fear God.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנן adds a teaching that fits the story of חזקיהו: do not stop praying even when it looks like death is certain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a very convincing dream that says you will die is not the final word. The פסוק teaches that dreams are full of empty things, so a person should put his trust in God, and that means he should keep praying.

keyTerms.meaning: The master of dreams, the one who shows a person a dream
Mercy; here it means praying to God for mercy
He should not hold himself back

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic lesson about prayer: no bad news, however certain it seems, is a reason to stop asking God for help.

steps.title: חזקיהו immediately turns to the wall and prays
steps.stepSummary: The story goes back to חזקיהו. Right after hearing ישעיהו's message that he would die, he turned to the wall and prayed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately, 'חזקיהו turned his face to the wall and prayed to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the story and quotes the פסוק showing that חזקיהו did not give up. He prayed right away. This also sets up the next question about the word 'wall.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'immediately' shows that חזקיהו acted just as רבי חנן taught. Even after a harsh prophecy he turned straight to prayer. The odd detail that he faced a wall is what the גמרא will ask about next.

phrases.english: Immediately, 'Chizkiyahu turned his face to the wall
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 38:2

phrases.english: and prayed to ה׳.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the story and shows חזקיהו doing what רבי חנן taught
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזקיהו responded to the prophecy of death by praying right away.

steps.title: What does the wall mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the פסוק means by saying חזקיהו turned to the 'wall.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'wall'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the word 'wall' in the פסוק. It is setting up two different answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would the פסוק bother to say he faced a wall? The גמרא assumes the detail must teach something, and it wants to know what.

phrases.english: What is meant by 'wall'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the פסוק just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word קיר (wall) in the פסוק about חזקיהו's prayer

steps.title: ריש לקיש: He prayed from the walls of his heart
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש explains that 'wall' points to the walls of חזקיהו's heart. He prayed from deep inside, and a פסוק in ירמיהו supports this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: From the walls of his heart, as it says: 'My insides, my insides, I writhe in pain; the walls of my heart...'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן לקיש gives the first answer: the 'wall' is not a real wall but the inner walls of the heart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He links the word קיר to the phrase קירות לבי, 'the walls of my heart,' in ירמיהו. So the פסוק is teaching that חזקיהו's prayer came from the very depths of his heart.

keyTerms.meaning: The walls of his heart, meaning his innermost feelings

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
From the walls of his heart,
as it is said: 'My insides, my insides, I writhe in pain;
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 4:19

phrases.english: the walls of my heart, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: מִקִּירוֹת לִבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question 'what is the wall?'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קיר hints at קירות לבו: חזקיהו prayed from the depths of his heart.

steps.title: רבי לוי: He mentioned a wall in his argument to God
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי says the wall refers to a real wall that חזקיהו brought up in his prayer. If the שונמית, who built only one small wall for אלישע, earned her son's life, then surely the descendant of שלמה, who covered the whole היכל in silver and gold, deserves to live.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: It is about matters of a wall. He said before God: Master of the World, if the שונמית, who made only one small wall, earned that You brought her son back to life, then my ancestor, who covered the entire היכל with silver and gold, how much more so!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי לוי gives a second answer: 'wall' hints at an argument חזקיהו made about a wall, using a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שונמית built a small walled room for אלישע and was rewarded when her son was brought back to life. חזקיהו argues that his ancestor שלמה did much more for God's house, so his descendant deserves even more to be saved. Unlike רבי שמעון בן לקיש, רבי לוי reads the wall as a real wall connected to a real story.

keyTerms.meaning: The woman from Shunem who hosted אלישע
How much more so; the phrase that finishes a קל וחומר

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the question 'what is the wall?'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קיר refers to the wall the שונמית built. חזקיהו used it in a קל וחומר to argue that the descendant of שלמה deserves to live.
steps.whatToRemember: Two ways to read 'wall': (1) רבי שמעון בן לקיש: he prayed from the walls of his heart. (2) רבי לוי: he argued from the שונמית's small wall, so how much more should the descendant of שלמה, who plated the היכל, be saved.

steps.title: The words of Chizkiyahu's prayer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק with חזקיהו's actual prayer: he asks God to remember that he walked before Him in truth and with a whole heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Please remember how I walked before You in truth and with a whole heart, and what is good in Your eyes I did.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues by quoting the words חזקיהו actually said in his prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the explanations of the 'wall,' the גמרא brings the next פסוק, where חזקיהו asks God to remember his loyal and sincere service. This continues the story and leads into what the גמרא will discuss next.

keyTerms.meaning: I walked before You, meaning I served You

phrases.english: 'Please remember how
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 38:3

phrases.english: I walked before You in truth
and with a whole heart,
and what is good in Your eyes I did.'

steps.triggerLanguage: ״זְכָר נָא אֵת אֲשֶׁר הִתְהַלַּכְתִּי לְפָנֶיךָ בֶּאֱמֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the story and quotes the content of חזקיהו's prayer
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזקיהו asked God to remember his truthful, wholehearted service.

steps.title: Which good deed did חזקיהו mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what specific deed חזקיהו meant when he said 'I did what is good in Your eyes.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'and I did what is good in Your eyes' refer to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא zooms in on the last words of חזקיהו's prayer and asks which good deed he was pointing to. This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his prayer, חזקיהו says he did 'what is good' in God's eyes, but the פסוק never says what that was. The גמרא assumes he meant one specific deed and wants to know which one.

keyTerms.meaning: And I did what is good in Your eyes

phrases.english: What is meant by 'and I did what is good in Your eyes'?
phrases.notes: These are the closing words of the prayer quoted in step 6 (ישעיהו 38:3).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the final phrase of the prayer quoted in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which specific good deed חזקיהו was referring to.

steps.title: רב: He placed גאולה right next to תפלה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, says the good deed was joining גאולה to תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: it means that he joined redemption to prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: חזקיהו's special deed was that he went straight from the גאולה blessing into his תפלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, the 'good' deed was a prayer habit. He did not stop between the blessing about redemption and the main prayer. That habit was important enough to mention when he asked for his life.

keyTerms.meaning: Redemption; the blessing after שמע that ends 'גאל ישראל'

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
That he joined redemption to prayer.
phrases.notes: He went from the blessing that ends 'גאל ישראל' straight into the עמידה, with no break.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The good deed was joining גאולה to תפלה.

steps.title: רבי לוי: He hid away the ספר רפואות
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי gives a different answer: the good deed was hiding away the Book of Remedies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: it means that he hid away the Book of Remedies.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer to the same question. רבי לוי says the good deed was that חזקיהו put the ספר רפואות out of use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי לוי ties the deed to a public act rather than a prayer habit. This answer also sets up the ברייתא that comes next, which lists hiding the ספר רפואות as one of חזקיהו's actions.

keyTerms.meaning: Hid away, put out of use

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi said:
That he hid away the Book of Remedies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 7's question, different from רב's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The good deed was hiding away the ספר רפואות.

steps.title: A ברייתא: Six things חזקיהו did
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says חזקיהו did six things. The חכמים agreed with three and disagreed with three.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: King חזקיהו did six things. On three they agreed with him, and on three they did not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that starts with a general headline: six actions, split into two groups of three. The next two steps fill in the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ספר רפואות from רבי לוי's answer leads into this teaching. The headline tells us the חכמים judged each of חזקיהו's actions on its own: some won their approval and some did not.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
King Hezekiah did six things;
on three they agreed with him,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the חכמים of his time.

phrases.english: and on three they did not agree with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי לוי's mention of the ספר רפואות with a ברייתא about חזקיהו's actions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזקיהו did six things. The חכמים approved three and did not approve three.

steps.title: The three actions the חכמים approved
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the three approved actions: hiding the ספר רפואות, crushing the copper snake, and giving his father a humble burial.
steps.simpleTranslation: On three they agreed with him: he hid away the Book of Remedies, and they agreed with him. He crushed the copper snake, and they agreed with him. He dragged his father's bones on a bed of ropes, and they agreed with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now names the first group, the three things the חכמים agreed with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these actions took away something that could lead people the wrong way or that did not deserve honor. The list starts with the ספר רפואות, which links back to רבי לוי's answer in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: A bed made of ropes (a plain bier)

phrases.english: On three they agreed with him:
He hid away the Book of Remedies, and they agreed with him.
He crushed the copper snake, and they agreed with him.
phrases.notes: This is the snake משה made in the desert (במדבר 21:9). People later served it like an idol (מלכים ב 18:4).

phrases.english: He dragged the bones of his father

phrases.aramaic: עַל מִטָּה שֶׁל חֲבָלִים — וְהוֹדוּ לוֹ.
phrases.english: on a bed of ropes, and they agreed with him.
phrases.notes: His father was the wicked king אחז. A plain rope bed means he did not give him a king's funeral.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first half of the headline from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hiding the ספר רפואות, crushing the copper snake, and giving אחז a humble burial were approved.

steps.title: The three actions the חכמים did not approve
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the three disapproved actions: blocking the גיחון waters, cutting off the doors of the היכל for the king of אשור, and making a leap month during ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: On three they did not agree with him: he stopped up the waters of the גיחון, and they did not agree with him. He cut off the doors of the היכל and sent them to the king of אשור, and they did not agree with him. He made ניסן a leap month while already in ניסן, and they did not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the list with the three actions the חכמים did not agree with. This closes the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists these actions without giving a reason for the disapproval. Together with step 11, it shows that even a righteous king like חזקיהו had some decisions the חכמים did not accept.

keyTerms.meaning: The waters of the גיחון spring
Made a leap year (added a month)

steps.whatToRemember: חזקיהו did six notable things. The חכמים approved three (ספר רפואות, the copper snake, אחז's burial) and did not approve three (the גיחון waters, the doors of the היכל, the leap month in ניסן).
steps.confusionAlert: The words עיבר ניסן בניסן make it sound as if he added a month after ניסן had already begun, and the next step asks exactly that. The גמרא's answer in step 14 is that he declared the leap year on the thirtieth of אדר, a day that could still become ניסן.

phrases.english: And on three they did not agree with him:

phrases.aramaic: סָתַם מֵי גִיחוֹן — וְלֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ.
phrases.english: He stopped up the waters of the Gihon, and they did not agree with him.
He cut off the doors of the Sanctuary

phrases.aramaic: וְשִׁגְּרָם לְמֶלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר — וְלֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ.
phrases.english: and sent them to the king of Assyria, and they did not agree with him.

phrases.aramaic: עִבֵּר נִיסָן בְּנִיסָן — וְלֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ.
phrases.english: He added a leap month for Nisan during Nisan, and they did not agree with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the second half of the headline from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blocking the גיחון, sending the doors of the היכל to אשור, and making a leap month in ניסן were not approved.

steps.title: How could חזקיהו add a second ניסן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how חזקיהו could make a leap month in ניסן, since the Torah says there is only one ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't חזקיהו know the פסוק 'This month shall be for you the first of the months'? That teaches: this is ניסן, and no other month is ניסן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last item in the ברייתא, where חזקיהו made a leap month during ניסן. It asks how a great king could break a clear Torah rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the פסוק we learn that once ניסן has started, you cannot add a second ניסן. If חזקיהו added an extra month during ניסן, he broke a Torah law, and that seems impossible for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't he hold / accept? (opens a challenge)
Making a leap year by adding a month
The first month of the Jewish year

phrases.english: But doesn't חזקיהו accept
"This month shall be for you the first of the months":
phrases.notes: שמות 12:2

phrases.english: This is ניסן, and no other month is ניסן?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the third disapproved action listed in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that חזקיהו made a leap month during ניסן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah says only one month is ניסן, so adding a second ניסן breaks a Torah rule. חזקיהו would not do that.

steps.title: חזקיהו declared the leap year on the thirtieth of אדר
steps.stepSummary: חזקיהו did not break the Torah rule. He declared the leap year on the thirtieth of אדר, which שמואל later said is not allowed because that day could become ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he made a mistake about the rule later taught by שמואל. שמואל said: you may not declare a leap year on the thirtieth day of אדר, since that day could be set as the first of ניסן. חזקיהו held that we do not use the reasoning of 'since it is fit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that חזקיהו did not add a month in the middle of ניסן. He declared it on the thirtieth of אדר, a day that might still turn into ראש חודש ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The thirtieth of אדר is not ניסן yet, but it could become ראש חודש ניסן if witnesses come. The חכמים said that 'it could become ניסן' is enough to forbid a leap year that day. חזקיהו held that a day that only might become ניסן is not treated as ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: Making the year a leap year
Since it is fit / could become
We do not say (we don't use this reasoning)

steps.whatToRemember: חזקיהו didn't add a month in real ניסן. He did it on the thirtieth of אדר, and the חכמים disagreed because that day could become ניסן.
steps.confusionAlert: שמואל lived long after חזקיהו. The גמרא means חזקיהו made a mistake about the rule that שמואל would later state, not that he argued with שמואל himself.

phrases.english: Rather, he erred regarding the rule of שמואל
phrases.notes: שמואל lived many generations later. This means the rule that שמואל would later say.

phrases.english: as שמואל said:
One may not make the year a leap year
on the thirtieth day of אדר,
since it is fit to be set as ניסן.
He held: "since it is fit" — we do not say that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 13 by redefining when חזקיהו made the leap year.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the leap year was declared on the thirtieth of אדר, not during ניסן itself.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חזקיהו added a second ניסן and broke a Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: He declared it on the thirtieth of אדר. He held that 'since it could become ניסן' is not a reason to forbid it, and the חכמים disagreed.

steps.title: Relying on your own merit or on others' merit
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי יוסי בן זמרא, teaches that someone who relies on his own merit is answered through others' merit, and someone who relies on others' merit is answered through his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי יוסי בן זמרא: Anyone who bases his request on his own merit is answered based on the merit of others. And anyone who bases his request on the merit of others is answered based on his own merit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the leap-year topic to a new teaching about how to ask ה׳ for things in prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a rule about humility in prayer. A person who points to his own good deeds ends up being helped because of others. A person who humbly points to others is helped because of his own merit.

keyTerms.meaning: One who relies / hangs his request on

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule fits the earlier story of חזקיהו's prayer and teaches the value of humility when asking ה׳ for help.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן זִמְרָא:
phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי יוסי בן זמרא:
Anyone who bases his request on his own merit —
is answered based on the merit of others.
And anyone who bases his request on the merit of others —
is answered based on his own merit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן זִמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the leap-year discussion and opens a new teaching about prayer, connected to the larger חזקיהו story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever relies on his own merit is answered through others' merit. Whoever relies on others' merit is answered through his own merit.

steps.title: Proof from משה
steps.stepSummary: משה prayed using the merit of the אבות, and the פסוק says the people were saved because of משה himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה relied on the merit of others, as it says: 'Remember אברהם, יצחק and ישראל, Your servants.' He was answered through his own merit, as it says: 'And He said He would destroy them, had not משה, His chosen one, stood in the breach before Him to turn back His anger from destroying.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the second half of רבי יוחנן's rule from משה's prayer after the חטא העגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his prayer, משה pointed only to the merit of the אבות. Yet תהלים says ה׳ held back from destroying the people because of משה himself. This shows that someone who relies on others' merit is answered in his own merit.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)
Stood in the breach (stood up to protect them)

phrases.english: משה relied on the merit of others,
as it says: "Remember אברהם, יצחק and ישראל, Your servants."
phrases.notes: שמות 32:13

phrases.english: He was answered based on his own merit,
as it says: "And He said He would destroy them,
had not משה, His chosen one,
stood in the breach before Him
to turn back His anger from destroying."
phrases.notes: תהלים 106:23

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a proof for the second half of the rule in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: Whoever relies on others' merit is answered in his own merit.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משה's prayer in שמות 32:13, compared with תהלים 106:23.

steps.title: חזקיהו relied on his own merit and was answered through others' merit
steps.stepSummary: חזקיהו asked to be saved because of his own good deeds, but הקב"ה answered him because of His own sake and the merit of דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיהו based his prayer on his own merit, as it says: 'Please remember how I walked before You.' But he was answered through the merit of others, as it says: 'I will protect this city to save it, for My sake and for the sake of דוד My servant.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second half of the proof for רבי יוחנן's rule. Here is someone who relied on his own merit and was answered through someone else's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 proved the second half of the rule: משה relied on the אבות and was answered for his own sake. Now חזקיהו proves the first half. He mentioned his own deeds, but the answer mentioned only הקב"ה and דוד, not חזקיהו.

keyTerms.meaning: He relied on his own merit

phrases.english: חזקיהו relied on his own merit,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״זְכָר נָא אֵת אֲשֶׁר הִתְהַלַּכְתִּי לְפָנֶיךָ״,
phrases.english: as it is written: 'Please remember how I walked before You,'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 38:3

phrases.english: and he was answered through the merit of others,
as it says: 'I will protect this city to save it'
for My sake and for the sake of דוד My servant.'
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 19:34. Notice that חזקיהו's own merit is not mentioned at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun with משה in step 16 by showing the opposite case.
steps.raayaObject: The first half of רבי יוחנן's rule: whoever relies on his own merit is answered through others' merit.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 38:3 (חזקיהו's prayer) together with מלכים ב 19:34 (God's answer).

steps.title: Why חזקיהו felt bitter even when he was healed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי reads the פסוק 'for my peace I had great bitterness' as describing חזקיהו's feelings when he was healed, but not through his own merit.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches what רבי יהושע בן לוי said. What does the פסוק 'Behold, for my peace I had great bitterness' mean? Even when הקב"ה sent him peace, it was bitter for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support from רבי יהושע בן לוי. He reads a פסוק as saying that חזקיהו was bitter even at the moment he was told he would recover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would someone feel bitter on hearing good news? Based on step 17, the answer is that the healing came through others' merit and not his own. So רבי יהושע בן לוי's reading fits the idea we just learned.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is the same as / this matches

phrases.english: And this matches what רבי יהושע בן לוי said.
For רבי יהושע בן לוי said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״הִנֵּה לְשָׁלוֹם מָר לִי מָר״ —
phrases.english: What is meant by what is written: 'Behold, for my peace I had great bitterness'?
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 38:17

phrases.english: Even at the time that He sent him
(that is, the Holy One, Blessed be He) peace,
phrases.notes: 'Peace' here means the good news that he would get well.

phrases.english: it was bitter for him.

steps.whatToRemember: חזקיהו relied on his own merit and was answered through others' merit. That is why even his healing felt bitter to him.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 17 by explaining חזקיהו's bitterness: he was saved, but not through his own merit.
steps.raayaObject: That חזקיהו was answered through others' merit and not his own.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע בן לוי's reading of ישעיהו 38:17.

steps.title: The פסוק about building a small room for אלישע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the woman from שונם's suggestion to build a small room on the roof for אלישע.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Let us please make a small chamber with walls.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a פסוק. This line sets up the next step, where רב and שמואל explain what kind of room it was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the unusual phrase עליית קיר, 'a chamber of wall.' The coming argument is about what this phrase means.

keyTerms.meaning: A chamber with walls, an upper room

phrases.english: 'Let us please make a small chamber with walls.'
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 4:10. The woman from שונם is speaking to her husband about a room for אלישע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a discussion of the שונמית's room, which רבי לוי mentioned in step 5 in his reading of חזקיהו's prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק to be explained: the woman from שונם built a 'small chamber with walls' for אלישע.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue about what the room was
steps.stepSummary: One says it was an open upper story that they roofed over. The other says it was a large enclosed porch that they split into two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל disagree. One said: it was an upper story with no roof, and they covered it. The other said: it was a large enclosed porch, and they divided it in two.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים explain the פסוק in different ways. Each one describes what was physically built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first view, the building work was adding a ceiling to a roof room that was open. In the second view, the work was adding a wall to split a big porch into two rooms. The גמרא does not say which אמורא holds which view.

keyTerms.meaning: And they roofed it / covered it

phrases.english: רב and שמואל: one said:
It was an uncovered upper story, and they put a roof over it.
And one said: it was a large enclosed porch,
and they divided it into two.

steps.confusionAlert: וְקֵירוּהָ here means 'they put a ceiling on it' (from קורה, a roof beam). It does not mean 'they built a wall.' That is exactly why the next step asks about the word קיר.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the פסוק quoted in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dispute: either an open roof room that was covered with a ceiling, or a large porch that was split in two.

steps.title: Where is the 'wall' according to the roofed-room view?
steps.stepSummary: The porch view explains the word קיר, since they built a dividing wall. But according to the open-roof view, what is the wall?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to the one who says it was a porch, because that is why the פסוק says 'wall.' But according to the one who says it was an upper story, what does 'wall' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first opinion. It points to a word in the פסוק that does not seem to fit that opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If they split a porch, they built a wall, so the word קיר fits well. If they only added a ceiling, no wall was built, so the word קיר seems to have no meaning. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (according to one view)
According to the one who says

phrases.english: It makes sense according to the one who says it was a porch:
that is why 'wall' is written,
but according to the one who says it was an upper story,
what is the meaning of 'wall'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the two opinions from step 20 against the wording of the פסוק in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that it was an uncovered upper story that was roofed over.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says קיר (wall), but that opinion has only a ceiling being added and no wall being built.

steps.title: The open-roof view reads קיר as 'they roofed it'
steps.stepSummary: The view that it was an open upper story explains the word קיר as coming from קירוי, roofing. They put a roof over it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They roofed it over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 21. According to the open-roof view, the word קיר does not mean a wall. It means they put a roof on the room.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that the open-roof view has no wall to point to, so the word קיר seemed out of place. The answer reads קיר as related to the word for roofing (קירוי). So the פסוק is describing the roof they added to the open upper story.

phrases.english: That they roofed it over.
phrases.notes: The word קיר in the פסוק is being read here as 'roofing' instead of 'wall.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21 against the open-roof view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קיר means a wall, which only fits the porch view.
steps.terutzMaskana: קיר can mean roofing, which fits the open-roof view.

steps.title: Challenge to the porch view: why call it an upper room?
steps.stepSummary: The word עליית fits the upper-story view. But if it was a porch, why does the פסוק call it an upper room?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says it was an upper story, because the פסוק says 'upper room.' But for the one who says it was a porch, what does 'upper room' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns the question around. It challenges the porch view using a different word in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each view now has a word that seems to fit only the other side. The open-roof view has just explained קיר. Now the word עליית ('upper room') looks like it supports only the upper-story view, because a porch is on the ground level.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (for one side, but not the other)
A porch or large covered hall
According to the one who says

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says it was an upper story,
that is why it is written 'upper room of'.
But according to the one who says it was a porch,
what is the meaning of 'upper room'?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר עֲלִיָּיה הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 21, this time questioning the porch view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that it was a porch split in two
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק calls it an 'upper room,' which seems to fit only a room on an upper floor.

steps.title: The porch view reads עליית as 'the finest room'
steps.stepSummary: The porch view explains עליית as 'the finest' (מעולה) of the rooms, not as an upper story.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means the finest of the rooms.
steps.whatsHappening: The porch view answers the challenge. It says עליית here means 'the best room,' not 'the upstairs room.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer reads the word עליית as related to מעולה, meaning excellent. So the פסוק is praising the room as the nicest in the house, not telling us which floor it was on. Now each view has explained the word that seemed to work against it.
steps.whatToRemember: Both views can explain the פסוק. The open-roof view reads קיר as 'roofing,' and the porch view reads עליית as 'the finest room.'

phrases.english: The 'finest' of the rooms.
phrases.notes: The word עליית is being read like מעולה, 'excellent,' so it means the best room in the house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עליית means an upper story, which only fits the open-roof view.
steps.terutzMaskana: עליית can mean 'the finest room,' which fits the porch view too.

steps.title: The furniture she placed in the room
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the פסוק: the woman from שונם planned to put a bed, a table, a chair and a lamp in the room.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And let us place there for him a bed, a table, a chair and a lamp.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next words of the woman from שונם. It is setting up the next discussion, which will look at these items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the argument about the room finished, the גמרא moves on to what she put inside it. The פסוק is quoted here as a base text. Its meaning will be discussed next.

phrases.english: 'And let us place for him there
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 4:10

phrases.english: a bed, a table, a chair and a lamp.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנָשִׂים לוֹ שָׁם מִטָּה וְשֻׁלְחָן וְכִסֵּא וּמְנוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the structure of the room to what was placed inside it, continuing the same פסוק from step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The woman from שונם planned to furnish אלישע's room with a bed, a table, a chair and a lamp.

steps.title: Accepting gifts: like אלישע or like שמואל
steps.stepSummary: אביי (or רבי יצחק) says a great person may choose to accept gifts like אלישע, or refuse them like שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי, and some say רבי יצחק, said: A person who wants to benefit from others may do so, like אלישע. A person who does not want to benefit should not, like שמואל from רמה.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the woman from שונם gave אלישע a room and furniture, the גמרא asks if it is fine for a great person to accept such gifts. אביי says both ways are fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אלישע accepted the woman's gifts, so taking them is allowed. שמואל never took anything from anyone, so refusing is also a proper path. Each great person can choose.

keyTerms.meaning: and some say (the statement belongs to a different rabbi)
the prophet hosted by the woman from שונם
the prophet שמואל from the town of רמה

phrases.english: Abaye said, and some say Rabbi Yitzchak:
One who wants to benefit may benefit, like Elisha.
And one who does not want to benefit should not benefit,
like Samuel from Ramah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The woman's plan to furnish a room for אלישע raises the question of a great person accepting gifts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A great person may accept gifts (like אלישע) or refuse them (like שמואל); both are proper.

steps.title: Proof that שמואל took nothing from anyone
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק says שמואל returned to רמה because his house was there; רבי יוחנן explains he brought his house wherever he went.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And his return was to רמה, for his house was there.' And רבי יוחנן said: Wherever he went, his house went with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that שמואל did not take gifts. It uses a פסוק about his house, as explained by רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'his house was there' seems obvious, so רבי יוחנן reads it as: he took all his own things along on every trip. That way he never needed to use anyone else's things.

keyTerms.meaning: his house (his belongings) was with him

phrases.english: As it is said: "And his return was to Ramah, for there was his house,"
phrases.notes: שמואל א ז:יז

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהָלַךְ שָׁם — בֵּיתוֹ עִמּוֹ.
phrases.english: Every place he went, his house was with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וּתְשׁוּבָתוֹ הָרָמָתָה כִּי שָׁם בֵּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second half of step 26: שמואל did not benefit from others.
steps.raayaObject: That שמואל refused to benefit from others.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק in שמואל א ז:יז, as read by רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatToRemember: Both paths are kosher: accepting gifts like אלישע, or living fully on your own like שמואל.

steps.title: A woman reads guests better than a man
steps.stepSummary: From the woman telling her husband that אלישע is holy, רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא learns that a woman recognizes guests better.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And she said to her husband: Behold, now I know that he is a holy man of God.' רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: From here we learn that a woman recognizes guests better than a man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the story's פסוקים. It learns a lesson from the fact that the wife, not the husband, noticed אלישע's greatness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She was the one who told her husband, so she saw it first. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא turns this into a general point: a woman senses a guest's character better.

phrases.english: "And she said to her husband:
phrases.notes: מלכים ב ד:ט

phrases.english: Behold now, I know
that he is a holy man of God,"
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
From here we learn that a woman recognizes guests
more than a man does.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַתֹּאמֶר אֶל אִישָׁהּ הִנֵּה נָא יָדַעְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to reading the פסוקים of the שונמית story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman recognizes the character of guests better than a man.

steps.title: How did she know he was holy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what she saw that made her say אלישע was holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He is holy': How did she know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question about the פסוק and sets up the next step, where רב and שמואל answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She said more than 'he is a prophet'; she said 'holy'. The גמרא wants to know what she actually saw.

phrases.english: "He is holy":
From where did she know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Zooms in on the word 'holy' from the פסוק in step 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What sign showed the woman that אלישע was holy.

steps.title: רב and שמואל: two signs of his holiness
steps.stepSummary: One says no fly ever passed over his table; the other says she never saw a stain of קרי on his white linen sheet.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל disagree. One said: She never saw a fly pass over his table. The other said: She spread a linen sheet on his bed and never saw a stain of קרי on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב and שמואל each give a different sign she noticed. The גמרא does not say which rabbi said which.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer is a miracle-like sign: even flies stayed away from his table. The second is a sign of personal purity: on white linen any stain shows, yet there was never any trace of a nighttime emission.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel disagree.
One said:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא רָאֲתָה זְבוּב עוֹבֵר עַל שֻׁלְחָנוֹ,
phrases.english: She never saw a fly pass over his table,
and the other said:

phrases.aramaic: סָדִין שֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן הִצִּיעָה עַל מִטָּתוֹ
phrases.english: She spread a linen sheet on his bed
and never saw a stain of emission on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either no fly ever came over his table, or his linen sheet always stayed clean.

steps.title: He is holy, but his servant is not
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא reads 'he is holy' as hinting that only אלישע was holy, not his servant גיחזי.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He is holy': רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: He is holy, but his servant is not holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the extra word 'he' in the פסוק. It shows that she also saw something about the servant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'HE is holy' points to one person, leaving out the servant traveling with him. This fits step 28: she read her guests well, both the holy one and the one who wasn't.

phrases.english: "He is holy"
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
He is holy, but his servant is not holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָדוֹשׁ הוּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another reading of the same words 'he is holy'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Her words 'he is holy' hint that אלישע was holy but גיחזי was not.

steps.title: Proof that גיחזי was not holy
steps.stepSummary: A later פסוק says גיחזי came to push her away; רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא reads it as touching her in an improper way.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And גיחזי came near to push her away.' רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: He grabbed her by the glory of her beauty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the servant was not holy, using a פסוק later in the story. A play on the word shows what he really did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word להדפה (to push her) is read as הוד יפיה (the glory of her beauty). This means that while pushing her, he touched her in an immodest way. So she was right about him.

phrases.english: As it is said: "And Geichazi approached to push her away,"
phrases.notes: מלכים ב ד:כז

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
He grabbed her by the glory of her beauty.
phrases.notes: A wordplay: להדפה sounds like הוד יפיה. He means גיחזי touched her immodestly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 31 by showing גיחזי's improper behavior.
steps.raayaObject: That גיחזי, the servant, was not holy.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים ב ד:כז, read through the wordplay להדפה = הוד יפיה.
steps.whatToRemember: The woman from שונם read both guests correctly: אלישע was holy, and his servant גיחזי was not.

steps.title: Hosting a Torah scholar is like bringing the daily offering
steps.stepSummary: From the words 'passes by us continually' (תמיד), רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, quoting רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, teaches that hosting a תלמיד חכם and letting him enjoy your things counts as if you brought תמידין.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the words 'who passes by us continually': רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: anyone who hosts a Torah scholar in his home and lets him benefit from his belongings is credited by the verse as if he were offering the daily sacrifices.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes one more phrase from the woman's description of אלישע and draws a lesson about hosting Torah scholars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman said אלישע passes by them 'תמיד' (continually). The word תמיד is also the name of the daily קרבן in the בית המקדש. So the verse hints that feeding and hosting a תלמיד חכם is counted like bringing the תמיד offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Continually; also the name of the daily קרבן
And lets him benefit from his belongings
The verse credits him as though

steps.whatToRemember: This closes the lessons from the woman of שונם: hosting a תלמיד חכם is counted like bringing the daily תמיד offering.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how much the גמרא values supporting Torah scholars. Giving them a place to stay is treated like a form of עבודה in the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: "Who passes by us continually"
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 4:9. These are still the woman's words about אלישע.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov:
Anyone who hosts a Torah scholar
in his home and lets him benefit from his belongings
the verse credits him
as if he were offering the daily sacrifices.
phrases.notes: This is a play on the word תמיד, which means 'continually' and is also the name of the daily קרבן.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹבֵר עָלֵינוּ תָּמִיד, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of readings of the woman's words about אלישע and finishes that series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hosting a תלמיד חכם and letting him enjoy one's belongings is credited as if one brought the תמיד offerings.

steps.title: Pray from a low place, not a high one
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, quoting רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, rules that a person should not pray standing in a high place but in a low place, based on 'from the depths I called You'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא also said in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: a person should not stand in a high place and pray. He should stand in a low place and pray, as it says: 'From the depths I called You, ה׳'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic, the הלכות of תפילה, quoting a new teaching from the same two Rabbis.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing here comes from the אלישע story anymore. The link is only that the teacher and the chain of names are the same. The פסוק describes calling to ה׳ 'from the depths', so the proper place for תפילה is a low spot.
steps.confusionAlert: This is a brand-new topic. It is not connected to the story of אלישע. The גמרא simply strings together several teachings said by the same Rabbis.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov:

phrases.aramaic: אַל יַעֲמוֹד אָדָם בְּמָקוֹם גָּבוֹהַּ וְיִתְפַּלֵּל,
phrases.english: A person should not stand in a high place and pray;
rather, he should stand in a low place and pray.
As it says: "From the depths I called You, Lord."
phrases.notes: תהלים 130:1

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב: אַל יַעֲמוֹד אָדָם בְּמָקוֹם גָּבוֹהַּ וְיִתְפַּלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, linked to the previous step only because it has the same chain of teachers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should pray in a low place, not a high place, as the פסוק says 'from the depths'.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports praying from a low place
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same rule: do not pray on a chair, a stool, or a high place, because there should be no haughtiness before ה׳. It brings two פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: a person should not stand on a chair, on a stool, or in a high place and pray. He should stand in a low place and pray, because there is no haughtiness before God. As it says, 'From the depths I called You, ה׳', and it is written, 'A prayer of the poor man when he is faint'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, to back up his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds two things. It gives specific examples (a chair, a stool), and it gives the reason: standing high shows pride, and pride does not belong before ה׳. It also adds a second פסוק that compares the one who prays to a poor man who humbly pours out his heart.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא; this introduces support
For a poor man when he is faint

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יַעֲמוֹד אָדָם לֹא עַל גַּבֵּי כִּסֵּא,
phrases.english: A person should not stand on top of a chair,
nor on top of a stool,
nor in a high place, and pray;
rather, he should stand in a low place and pray.
Because there is no haughtiness before God.
As it says: "From the depths I called You, Lord."
And it is written: "A prayer of the poor man when he is faint."
phrases.notes: תהלים 102:1

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the rule in step 34 with a ברייתא that also adds the reason behind it.
steps.raayaObject: The rule of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא that one should pray from a low place.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that bans praying on a chair, a stool, or a high place, explains that pride does not belong before ה׳, and cites תהלים 130:1 and 102:1.

steps.title: Line up your feet when you pray
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, quoting רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, rules that one who prays must line up his feet, learning it from the description of the angels' feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא also said in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: one who prays must line up his feet, as it says: 'And their feet were a straight foot'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching about תפילה from the same Rabbis: how to place your feet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes the angels' feet as 'one straight foot'. From this we learn that during תפילה a person should put his feet together so they look like a single foot, like the angels.

keyTerms.meaning: That he should line up his feet

steps.whatToRemember: Two rules about how to stand for תפילה: stand in a low place, showing humility, and put your feet together like the angels.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known practice of standing with feet together during שמונה עשרה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov:
One who prays must line up his feet,
phrases.notes: He means putting the feet right next to each other, so they look like one foot.

phrases.english: as it says: "And their feet were a straight foot."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 1:7, describing the angels.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב: הַמִּתְפַּלֵּל צָרִיךְ שֶׁיְּכַוֵּין אֶת רַגְלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second rule about how to stand during תפילה, from the same chain of teachers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who prays must place his feet together, like the angels whose feet are 'a straight foot'.

steps.title: Do not eat before praying for your life
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, reads the פסוק 'Do not eat on the blood' as 'Do not eat before you pray for your blood,' meaning your life.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: What does the פסוק 'You shall not eat on the blood' mean? It means: do not eat before you have prayed for your blood, which is your life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more teaching from the same chain of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא quoting רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. He reads a פסוק as a rule that you must pray before you eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply read, the פסוק is about eating blood or eating near blood. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads 'the blood' as 'your blood,' meaning your life, and 'על' as 'for.' So the פסוק becomes: don't eat until you have prayed for your life.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall not eat on the blood' (ויקרא 19:26)
What is the meaning of what is written?

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source used for the practical halacha that a person should not eat a meal in the morning before שחרית.

phrases.english: (Rabbi Yitzchak said that Rabbi Yochanan said)
phrases.notes: The words in round brackets are in the printed גמרא, but some versions leave them out here.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov:
What is meant by what is written, 'You shall not eat on the blood'?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:26

phrases.english: Do not eat before
you pray for your blood.
phrases.notes: 'Your blood' here means your life. You pray for your life before you take care of feeding yourself.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דִּכְתִיב, לֹא תֹאכְלוּ עַל הַדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of teachings from רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב about how to pray.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not eat before praying.

steps.title: Another version: eating before praying is like casting ה׳ behind you
steps.stepSummary: In a second version of the teaching, one who eats and drinks and only then prays is described by the פסוק 'And Me you have cast behind your back.' It is read as 'behind your pride': only after satisfying his ego did he accept מלכות שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the teaching went like this: Anyone who eats and drinks and only afterward prays, the פסוק says about him, 'And Me you have cast behind your back.' Do not read 'your back' (גַּוֶּיךָ). Read it as 'your pride' (גֵּאֶיךָ‎). ה׳ says: only after this person puffed himself up did he accept upon himself מלכות שמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the same teaching, using the formula איכא דאמרי. This time the point comes through a different פסוק and a wordplay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version gave a rule from a פסוק in the תורה: don't eat before praying. This version gives a harsh rebuke instead. Putting your own food first is pride, and it puts ה׳ 'behind' you. The change from גַּוֶּיךָ to גֵּאֶיךָ turns 'back' into 'pride.'

keyTerms.meaning: Some say: introduces another version of a teaching
'And Me you have cast behind your back' (מלכים א 14:9)
Do not read it as ... but as ...: a wordplay reading
The kingship of Heaven, accepting ה׳ as King

steps.confusionAlert: The 'אל תקרי' is not changing the פסוק itself. It is a way of drawing an extra lesson from a similar-sounding word.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree: a person should not eat before תפילה. The first version gives it as a rule from the תורה, and the second as a rebuke against pride.

phrases.english: There are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said that Rabbi Yochanan said
that Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov:
Anyone who eats and drinks
and afterward prays,
about him the פסוק says:
'And Me you have cast behind your back.'
phrases.notes: מלכים א 14:9

phrases.english: Do not read 'your back' but 'your pride.'
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Only after this one became proud
did he accept upon himself the kingdom of Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of the teaching in step 37, with the same message but a different פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating and drinking before praying is an act of pride that puts ה׳ 'behind' oneself.

steps.title: The halacha follows רבי יהושע: until three hours
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, quoting רבי יהושע that the morning שמע may be said until three hours. רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules the halacha like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: רבי יהושע says the morning שמע may be said until three hours into the day. רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the halacha follows רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The long side discussion is over, and the גמרא goes back to the words of the משנה. It gives a final ruling that we follow רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה had a disagreement about how late the morning שמע may be said. שמואל settles it: the halacha follows רבי יהושע, who allows until the end of the third hour of the day.

keyTerms.meaning: Until three hours into the day
The halacha follows ...: the practical ruling
רב יהודה quoting his teacher שמואל

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling for the latest time to say the morning קריאת שמע.
steps.whatToRemember: The morning שמע may be said until the end of three hours of the day, following רבי יהושע.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר עַד שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁעוֹת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: until three hours.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה, about how late you may say the morning שמע.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the series of teachings about תפילה and returns to the משנה about the time for קריאת שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The halacha follows רבי יהושע: the morning שמע may be said until three hours.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: one who reads later has not lost
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: one who says שמע after this time has not lost. This sets up an explanation of what that means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: one who reads שמע from this point on has not lost.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה. It is setting up the next move, where it will explain what 'has not lost' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading after three hours is past the set time. Yet the משנה says the person 'has not lost.' This leaves a question the גמרא will now answer: what exactly does he still gain?
steps.confusionAlert: 'Has not lost' does not mean he did the מצוה at its proper time. The גמרא is about to explain what he does gain.

phrases.english: One who reads from this point onward
phrases.notes: This is another quote from our משנה. 'This point' means after the three hours.

phrases.english: has not lost.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the משנה right after the ruling about רבי יהושע, to set up the next explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading שמע after three hours still has some value: the reader 'has not lost.'

steps.title: No blessings after the time
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, in the name of מר עוקבא, limits the משנה: someone who says שמע late has not lost, but he may not say the ברכה of יוצר אור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of מר עוקבא: He has not lost, but only on condition that he does not say 'Who forms light.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the משנה's line 'he has not lost.' רב חסדא adds a limit: a person who says שמע late should not say the ברכות that go with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that someone who says שמע after three hours has not lost. רב חסדא says that only the reading itself is still worthwhile. The ברכות, starting with יוצר אור, are tied to the proper time of שמע, so after that time he should leave them out.

keyTerms.meaning: Only on condition that; provided that
'Who forms light': the first ברכה before the morning שמע
An early אמורא; רב חסדא is quoting him here

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said that Mar Ukva said:
Provided that he does not say 'Who forms light.'
phrases.notes: He means the ברכות of שמע. 'Who forms light' is just the first one, standing in for all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and limits the משנה's line 'he has not lost' that was quoted in step 40.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the time of שמע has passed, a person may still read שמע but may not say its ברכות.

steps.title: A ברייתא says he does say the blessings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא with a ברייתא that says the late reader does say two ברכות before שמע and one after.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: One who reads from that time onward has not lost. He is like someone reading from the Torah. But he does say two blessings before it and one after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that seems to say the exact opposite of רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said the late reader may not say the ברכות. The ברייתא openly says he does say all of them: two before שמע and one after. A ברייתא is a teaching of the תנאים, so an אמורא like רב חסדא cannot argue with it.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection, usually from a ברייתא or משנה
From here onward; after the proper time
Two ברכות before the morning שמע and one after it

phrases.english: They raised an objection: One who reads from that time onward

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִפְסִיד, כְּאָדָם שֶׁהוּא קוֹרֵא בַּתּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: has not lost; he is like a person reading from the Torah,
but he does say two blessings before it
and one after it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב חסדא's ruling from step 41.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that the late reader may not say יוצר אור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא openly says the late reader says two ברכות before שמע and one after, which is the opposite of רב חסדא's ruling.

steps.title: רב חסדא's view is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רב חסדא's ruling has been disproved.
steps.simpleTranslation: The refutation of רב חסדא is a real refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits there is no answer, so רב חסדא's ruling, in this version, is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תיובתא means the question was too strong to answer. The final ruling follows the ברייתא: even after three hours, a person still says the ברכות of שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation: the view is disproved and there is no answer

steps.whatToRemember: In this first version, רב חסדא said 'no ברכות after the time,' and he was disproved. The ברייתא rules that one still says the ברכות.

phrases.english: The refutation of Rav Chisda is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of step 42 with no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב חסדא's limit is rejected. A person who says שמע late still says its ברכות.

steps.title: Second version: he has not lost the blessings
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רב חסדא in the name of מר עוקבא explains 'he has not lost' to mean that the late reader has not lost the ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב חסדא said that מר עוקבא said: What does 'he has not lost' mean? It means he has not lost the blessings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of what רב חסדא said. In this version he reads the משנה the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the words 'he has not lost' in the משנה are exactly about the ברכות. The late reader still keeps the right to say them. So רב חסדא now agrees with the ברייתא, and the earlier refutation does not apply to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say; a second version of a teaching
The blessings, here the ברכות of שמע

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions are said in רב חסדא's name, but they say opposite things. The first version was disproved; the second fits the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said that Mar Ukva said:
What is meant by 'he has not lost'?
That he has not lost the blessings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, opposite version of רב חסדא's teaching from step 41.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's 'he has not lost' means the late reader still says the ברכות of שמע.

steps.title: The ברייתא supports the second version
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא that refuted the first version now supports the second version.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: One who reads from that time onward has not lost. He is like someone reading from the Torah. But he does say two blessings before it and one after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that a ברייתא backs up the second version of רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the very ברייתא that disproved the first version. Here it works as a support, because it says the late reader does say the ברכות, just as the second version claims.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא; this brings support

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions end the same way in practice: a person who says שמע after three hours still says two ברכות before it and one after.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
One who reads from that time onward has not lost;
he is like a person who reads from the Torah,
but he does say two blessings before it
and one after it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second version from step 44.
steps.raayaObject: The second version of רב חסדא: the late reader has not lost the ברכות
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא saying the late reader says two ברכות before שמע and one after

steps.title: Saying שמע on time is greater than Torah study
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני teaches that someone who says קריאת שמע at its proper time is greater than someone who is learning Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מני said: Someone who reads קריאת שמע at its proper time is greater than someone who is busy learning Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement: רבי מני praises saying שמע at the right time and ranks it above Torah study.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying שמע is reading words of Torah, but on time it is also its own מצוה. So the person who says it on time gains more than someone who is only learning Torah. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is busy learning Torah

phrases.english: Rabbi Mani said:
Greater is one who reads קריאת שמע at its proper time
than one who is busy learning Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברכות to a new point about the value of saying שמע on time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying קריאת שמע at its proper time is greater than Torah study.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה's wording
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני proves his point: the משנה compares the late reader to a Torah learner, so the on-time reader must be greater.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the משנה teaches: One who reads after that time has not lost, and he is like a person reading from the Torah, we learn that one who reads at the proper time is better.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מני shows where his idea comes from: the משנה's own words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the late reader is like someone learning Torah. If the late reader only equals a Torah learner, then the person who says שמע on time must be on a higher level. That higher level is reading שמע on time, which is more than Torah study alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it teaches; an inference from the wording

steps.whatToRemember: The late reader of שמע is like someone learning Torah. The one who reads on time is greater.

phrases.english: Since it teaches:
One who reads from that time onward has not lost;
he is like a person reading from the Torah.
This implies that one who reads at its proper time is better.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the proof for רבי מני's statement in step 46.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מני's claim that saying שמע on time is greater than Torah study
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's comparison of the late reader to 'a person reading from the Torah'

steps.title: בית שמאי: Lie down at night, stand in the morning
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens with the view of בית שמאי: at night a person must recline to say שמע, and in the morning he must stand, based on "ובשכבך ובקומך".
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: בית שמאי say: In the evening, every person should lie on his side and say שמע. In the morning he should stand, because the פסוק says: "When you lie down and when you rise."
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, and it opens with בית שמאי's rule about the body position for saying שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי read "ובשכבך ובקומך" as telling us HOW to say שמע. Lying down matches "when you lie down" at night, and standing matches "when you rise" in the morning.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks where the text of the משנה begins
He should recline, lie on his side
"And when you lie down and when you rise", from the פסוק of שמע

phrases.english: MISHNA
Beit Shammai say:
In the evening, every person should recline and recite.
And in the morning he should stand,
as it is said: "When you lie down and when you rise."
phrases.notes: דברים 6:7

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: בָּעֶרֶב — כָּל אָדָם יַטֶּה וְיִקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It moves on from the discussion of reading שמע late to the question of body position.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, שמע at night must be said lying on one's side, and in the morning it must be said standing.

steps.title: בית הלל: Say it in any position
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל rule that each person says שמע in whatever position he is in, proven from "ובלכתך בדרך".
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל say: Every person says שמע in his normal way, in whatever position he is in, because the פסוק says: "And when you walk on the way."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposing view of בית הלל: no special position is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל point to a different part of the same פסוק: "ובלכתך בדרך". Someone walking on the road is neither lying down nor standing still, so the תורה must allow saying שמע in any position.

keyTerms.meaning: In his own way, as he normally is
"And when you walk on the way"

steps.whyThisMatters: The הלכה follows בית הלל, so in practice a person may say שמע sitting, standing, or walking.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say:
Every person recites in his own way.
as it is said: "And when you walk along the way."
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק, דברים 6:7.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: כָּל אָדָם קוֹרֵא כְּדַרְכּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to בית שמאי's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית הלל, שמע may be said in any position.

steps.title: Then why does the פסוק mention lying down and rising?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה challenges בית הלל: if position does not matter, what do the words "ובשכבך ובקומך" come to teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say "When you lie down and when you rise"?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks a question on בית הלל, and this sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי built their whole rule on "ובשכבך ובקומך". If בית הלל say position does not matter, those words seem to have no purpose. So בית הלל must explain them in some other way.

keyTerms.meaning: Why was it said?; what do these words come to teach?

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: If בית הלל are right that any position is fine.

phrases.english: why is it said: "When you lie down and when you rise"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions בית הלל's view using the very words בית שמאי relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's rule that position does not matter
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If position does not matter, the words "ובשכבך ובקומך" seem to teach nothing.

steps.title: The words teach the time, not the position
steps.stepSummary: "ובשכבך ובקומך" means the time when people go to sleep and the time when people get up.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means: at the time when people lie down to sleep, and at the time when people get up.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers for בית הלל: the words tell us WHEN to say שמע, not HOW to sit or stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל read "ובשכבך ובקומך" as a time marker: at night when people go to bed, and in the morning when people wake up. This way the words still have a purpose, and the body position stays open.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as בית הלל saying you must lie down at night. For בית הלל, "lie down" and "rise" only describe the TIME of day; your own position does not matter.
steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי: the פסוק teaches the position and the time. בית הלל: the פסוק teaches only the time (bedtime and waking time), and you may say שמע in any position.

phrases.english: At the time when people lie down
and at the time when people rise.
phrases.notes: Here עומדים means getting up from sleep in the morning, not standing on your feet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 50.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "ובשכבך ובקומך" describes the body position for saying שמע.
steps.terutzMaskana: For בית הלל, "ובשכבך ובקומך" describes the times of day: when people go to sleep and when they wake up.

steps.title: רבי טרפון reclined on the road and faced danger
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון tells how he lay down on the road to say שמע like בית שמאי and was put in danger by bandits.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון said: I was once traveling on the road, and I lay down to say שמע following בית שמאי, and I put myself in danger because of the bandits.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a true story from רבי טרפון about trying to follow בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון stopped on the road and lay down so he would follow בית שמאי's rule too. Lying on a road made him an easy target for bandits. The story shows that being extra strict like בית שמאי put his life at risk.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who tells this story
I reclined, I lay down on my side

steps.whatToRemember: רבי טרפון tried to follow בית שמאי by lying down on the road, and it put him in danger from bandits.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon said:
I was coming along the road
and I reclined to recite
according to the words of Beit Shammai.
And I endangered myself
because of the bandits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן: אֲנִי הָיִיתִי בָּא בַּדֶּרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a real-life story about acting like בית שמאי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lying down on the road to follow בית שמאי put רבי טרפון in danger from bandits.

steps.title: The Sages rebuke רבי טרפון for following בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The Sages tell רבי טרפון that he deserved to be in danger of losing his life, because he went against the words of בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: You deserved to lose your life, because you went against the words of בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The Sages answer רבי טרפון's story. They tell him that the danger he faced was his own fault, because he followed בית שמאי instead of בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון probably thought he was being extra careful by lying down like בית שמאי. The Sages say the opposite: since the הלכה follows בית הלל, acting like בית שמאי is not extra credit but going against the accepted ruling. So the danger was a fitting result of his choice.

keyTerms.meaning: You deserved it; it would have been fitting for you
To be liable with your own self, meaning to lose your life
You went against the words (ruling) of

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows בית הלל: you say שמע in whatever position you are in. Being strict like בית שמאי here is treated as going against the הלכה, not as extra piety.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי טרפון earned extra credit for being strict. The Sages say that following בית שמאי against בית הלל is itself a wrong act.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story shows that once the הלכה is decided like בית הלל, choosing בית שמאי's stricter way is not allowed. That idea matters well beyond this one case.

phrases.english: They said to him:
phrases.notes: "They" are the Sages, answering רבי טרפון's story from the previous step.

phrases.english: You deserved to be liable with your own life,
because you went against the words of בית הלל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: כְּדַי הָיִיתָ לָחוּב בְּעַצְמְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds directly to רבי טרפון's story in step 52 and rejects his choice to follow בית שמאי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows בית הלל, and acting like בית שמאי against them is considered going against the הלכה, deserving serious consequences.
